title: World Snooker Championship to remain at Crucible until 2045 as £45m revamp planned
content:
The World Snooker Championship is to remain in Sheffield until at least 2045, with the city’s historic Crucible Theatre venue set for a £45 million ($60m) revamp.

There had been doubts over whether the sport’s premier event would stay in the northern English city, with Saudi Arabia and China mooted as possible new destinations which could offer larger, more lucrative venues.

However, a deal has been struck to keep the tournament, which takes place every April, at the Crucible until 2045 with an option to extend to 2050.

Up to 500 seats will be added to the venue, increasing the capacity by around 50 per cent. The World Championship will temporarily move to an as-yet unspecified location while work takes place from the 2028 tournament onwards, with no timeframe put on the refurbishments.

Most of the redevelopment (£35m) will be publicly funded, with around £10m coming from private investment.

The World Championship has been held at the iconic Crucible since 1977 and the current agreement runs until 2027.

Barry Hearn, president of Matchroom Sport, which helps promote and run snooker, had previously labelled the venue as unfit for purpose.

In a release on Tuesday, Hearn said of the new agreement: “I am so happy that after a long period of meetings and discussions we have finally agreed a deal to stage the World Championship at its historic home — the Crucible.

“My thanks must go to Sheffield City Council for all of their hard work in ensuring this great tournament remains at its spiritual home.”

UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said: “I had the pleasure of recently visiting Sheffield, the home of the oldest football club in the world, to encourage partners to support a major redevelopment of the iconic Crucible Theatre to keep sport and culture thriving in this city.

“I’m delighted with today’s confirmation that the theatre and the city will stay host to the famous World Snooker Championships for many years to come.”

This year’s World Championship starts on April 18, when Zhao Xintong will look to defend the title he won last year, becoming the first Chinese winner of the event in the process.
